reference: Skogestad S. Simple analytic rules for model reduction and PID controller tuning. J Process Control. 2003;13:291–309. Corrected open reprint: Modeling, Identification and Control. 2004;25:85–120.
scope: Fully specified general integrating-process PI reference. Not a clinical CPB controller or medical device reproduction.
locations: Author notes: integrating process, original c=4, tau_c/theta=1
application_changes: Reservoir signed integrating gain is -1/60 L per second per L/min of outflow command
Nominal effective delay is half the 2-second actuator lag plus half the 1-second sample period; a design approximation, not identification from data
Both controllers share an oxygen-demand cap, pressure slowdown at 90 mmHg, 0–7 L/min command bounds and 0.15 L/min/s slew
PI reservoir override uses explicit tracking anti-windup after the shared application constraints
The same sensor/reference/observer pipeline feeds both methods, including the same optional noisy venous-flow channel
Forecast retains its own internal objective and candidate constraints. These are algorithm differences; comparison tuning uses a common outcome criterion
replication_claim: Published PI tuning and normalized frequency-domain example only. CPB application is a declared simulation adaptation. No original clinical traces or clinical validation are claimed.
previous_bypass_reference: Takahashi et al. remains an incomplete, separately labeled workbench; it is not used as the verified primary comparator.
